newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha easier on crudes, spreads narrower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha easier on crudes, spreads narrower.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha took a dive in afternoon Tokyo trade on Wednesday due to a plunge in crude oil prices on overnight overseas markets, traders said.
Naphtha prices had remained firm in east Asia over the past few days despite crude losses, amid tight supplies for prompt cargoes.
First-half February open-spec naphtha was indicated at $243.00/245.00, up from Tuesday's $250.00/251.00.
Second-half February was notionally quoted at $239.00/240.00, compared with $245.00/246.00 in late Tuesday trade.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half March was sold twice at $241.00 to Japanese trading houses and at $241.50 to a Western trader in Tuesday trade.

Also on Tuesday, first-half April changed hands at $233.50 between a Western trader and a Japanese trading house. Inter-delivery naphtha spreads narrowed slightly in reaction to losses in open-spec naphtha prices, with first-half February/first-half March discussed at plus $9.00/10.00.
It was traded twice at plus $10.00 and once at $11.00 earlier this week, traders said.
